summary: A funded collar is not possible for CBA Board directors, Group Company Secretaries, Group Executives or their Associates: para 9 bans any transaction that limits the economic risk of their exposure to any vested Group Securities, and para 16(a) bans using Group Securities as security for margin lending or any other secured financing. For other Specified Persons (e.g. Executive General Managers, Subsidiary Board directors, Group Control Room staff), the hedge leg over vested shares free of any holding lock is not expressly banned, but the OTC options are Securities and entering them is a Trade, so it must be done in a Trading Window, with Pre-Clearance where designated on the Conflicts Hub (valid three business days), subject to the 30-day LIFO holding rule, and it must not involve CFDs, short selling or stock lending of Group Securities. The loan leg secured on the collared shares is prohibited for all Specified Persons, so at most an unsecured or unfunded collar is workable for that group, and exercise or settlement mechanics that execute outside a Trading Window are a further risk under para 11. Employees who are not Specified Persons face only the insider trading prohibition and whatever Pre-Clearance the unpublished Procedure imposes. The MAR overlay in para 18 adds an outright bar for the senior group on any Security that prices off a UK/EU-listed Group Security.

summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy, which is a short 2011 insider-trading document with no substantive prohibitions on hedging, derivatives, margin lending or secured financing. Both collar legs are PME Securities because the definition expressly captures equity swaps, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options, cash-settled or not, so entering, rolling, unwinding and settling the collar are each Dealings that require prior written notice of intention to the Company Secretary, a written confirmation of no Inside Information, and advice from the Company Secretary that there is no known reason to preclude the Dealing, with execution inside 7 days. Dealings must fall within one of the three 30-day Trading Windows after the full-year results, half-year results and AGM, outside the two four-week Blackout Periods and any ad hoc Blackout the Board or Chairman declares, and the Chairman may shorten a window or bar an individual; out-of-window execution needs the Chairman's (or for the Chairman, the Board's) approval on exceptional circumstances such as severe financial hardship, subject to any conditions including disclosure. The secured loan is not itself a Dealing and is not prohibited, but full details of any margin lending or other security arrangement affecting the shares must be reported in writing to the Company Secretary after the Dealing, and directors must also meet their notifiable interest obligations and their letter agreement with the company. The main residual risks are the narrow dealing calendar with no forced-sale carve-out, and the rules of the Pro Medicus Share and Option Plans, which are incorporated by reference and may impose hedging or encumbrance restrictions on plan shares that this policy does not.

summary: A funded collar is not possible for IAG Specified Persons, the population that includes the directors and executives a bank would target. Clause 34, added by the 30 November 2023 amendment, prohibits Specified Persons and their Closely Related Parties from using IAG Securities as collateral in any financial transaction, with margin lending and transfers into a margin account given only as examples, and no approver has power to waive it. The derivative legs alone are also constrained: instruments that limit economic risk are themselves IAG Securities, so entry, roll and unwind each require a Trading Consent Request approved by the Group General Counsel & Company Secretary (or, for Non-Executive Directors, the more senior approver route), inside one of the three roughly 20 business day Trading Windows, valid for only 5 business days, subject to the front page test whose refusal is final and confidential, and subject to the three-month short-term trading ban. Plan shares can never be hedged before vesting or while under a holding lock, so only fully vested unrestricted shares are candidates, and any price-triggered or conditional feature must be both placed and executed within a window. A collar could in principle be offered on an unsecured basis over vested unrestricted shares, and Directors, Employees and Contractors who are not Specified Persons are not caught by clauses 30 or 34 at all, but for the target population the funded structure is barred.

summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy. Section 11.1 prohibits Directors, KMP and Employees from trading in any financial products issued or created over the Company's securities, which captures both the purchased put and the written call whether traded OTC or on exchange, with no clearance route, no exceptional-circumstances relief and no distinction by vesting state. summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy, and this is one of the more permissive ASX policies for the purpose. There is no hedging prohibition at all: products that limit the economic risk of holding SGH shares are simply defined as SGH securities, so the put and call legs are dealings that a designated employee may execute inside one of the three 30-working-day window periods following the half year results, annual results and AGM, or outside a window with prior written clearance from the approver named in the section 3 table. Margin lending is likewise expressly permitted with written clearance, which may be granted subject to conditions, and a disposal by a secured lender exercising its rights is carved out of the policy entirely provided the facility itself was cleared, which protects the bank on enforcement. The two hard constraints are that no Executive or designated staff member may deal in any financial product issued or created over or in respect of SGH securities during a blackout period, with no exceptional circumstances relief, and that clearance lapses after two business days, so the trade must be fully documented before approval is sought. summary: A funded collar is realistically achievable under this policy, which is markedly more permissive than most ASX policies on the financing leg. There is no prohibition on margin lending, secured financing, pledging or encumbering Lynas securities, granting security is not within the definition of Deal In Securities, and paragraph 8.1(6) expressly excludes from the policy a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights, so the bank's enforcement sale would not put the executive in breach even in a closed period. The derivative legs are the constraint: a put and call over Lynas shares are financial products created over the Company's securities and cannot be traded during prohibited periods (14.1), and since 7.3 makes every period a closed period except the three weeks following results, the AGM or a prospectus, entry, roll, unwind and settlement must each be timed into one of those narrow windows and preceded by written confirmation of no impediment from the Chairman (directors) or Secretary (employees). The 13.2 hedging ban reaches only employee options before vesting, so vested shares may be collared, but the undefined at all times ban on short-term trading in 13.1 argues for a long tenor and for clearing the structure explicitly. Out-of-window relief under 9.2 covers only a sale of securities, not derivative dealings, so no exceptional-circumstances route exists for an emergency unwind, and directors should expect the position to surface through immediate notification to the company secretary and an Appendix 3Y.

summary: A funded collar is close to workable at BlueScope but is defeated by the financing leg as ordinarily documented. The derivative legs are unusually accommodating: the policy names a 'cap or collar facility' and third party put and call options in the list of restricted trading rather than in a prohibition, so a Restricted Person may enter a collar over vested, unrestricted shares provided it is done inside one of the three trading windows (45 days after each of the half year and full year results, and 15 days after the AGM), after written notice to the Company Secretary, confirmation of no inside information and written clearance, which is valid for 10 trading days and revocable at any time. The loan leg is the problem: Restricted Persons must not enter into any new arrangement pledging BlueScope Steel securities as collateral for a loan or other agreement which could permit a sale without the holder's consent, with no clearance route and no exemption authority, and any resulting forced sale is a breach for which exceptions will expressly not be considered. The prohibition is conditional rather than absolute, so a structure in which the bank has no independent power of sale over the collared shares is the only route worth exploring. Two further constraints apply: nothing may be hedged while unvested or within a restriction period, and the nine month short-term trading ban means the collar tenor and the seasoning of the underlying shares must both exceed nine months.

summary: A funded collar is realistically achievable at WiseTech, which is one of the more permissive policies in the market. Hedging is banned only for plan securities that are unvested or subject to a holding lock or plan dealing restriction, so vested unrestricted shares, including shares bought on market, may be hedged; the derivative legs would be a dealing requiring only prior notification to the Company Secretary and the Chair for a Director (with a 5 business day window and a same-day post-trade confirmation), or approval on a Clearance to Trade Request Form for other Restricted Persons, answered typically within one business day. The funding leg is likewise available: the only financing rule is that a margin lending arrangement, or a transfer of shares into an existing margin loan account, needs approval under section 5.5, and the Company may impose conditions on that approval, notably about when shares may be sold to satisfy a margin call; there is no encumbrance ban, no vesting restriction on collateral and no financier disclosure obligation. Critically, section 6(e) treats a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights as an Excluded Dealing outside the short-term trading ban, the blackout periods and the notification and approval requirements, so a bank enforcement sale does not put the executive in breach. The practical conditions are that entry falls outside the 30 June and 31 December blackout periods and any Board-specified or Company-notified dealing ban, that the tenor and the seasoning of the underlying shares both exceed six months to avoid the short-term dealing rule, and that the structure is disclosed and cleared on a substance over form basis, since the Company can condition its approval on the enforcement mechanics of the loan.

However, section 5.2 flatly prohibits Restricted Persons from entering into margin lending arrangements in relation to the Company's securities, with no approval route, and the express substance over form principle means a bank facility secured on the collared shares with LVR or margin call mechanics is likely to be treated as such, so a funded structure would need to be demonstrably not a margin lending arrangement. Tenor is a further constraint: forward contracts are expressly given as an example of a prohibited short term dealing and buying and selling within 90 days is banned, so the collar should run well beyond 90 days. summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy, which is one of the more permissive on the ASX. Section 5.4(d) expressly permits Employees and their Connected Persons to hedge vested and unrestricted Company securities, provided the hedge is treated as a dealing: prior approval through trading@netwealth.com.au from the Joint Managing Directors (Senior Executives and Nominated Employees), the Chair of the Board (directors) or the Chair of the Compliance and Risk Management Committee (the Chair), execution within five business days, no dealing in the 30 June or 31 December blackout periods or any Board-specified period, no Inside Information at entry, renewal, alteration or close-out, and prompt post-trade confirmation. The loan leg is likewise an approval regime rather than a ban: section 5.3 requires approval for entering a margin lending arrangement over Netwealth securities, transferring shares into the lender's account and selling shares to meet a call, and the approver may impose conditions on when the collateral may be sold, while section 6(e) puts a secured lender's enforcement sale outside the blackout, approval and short-term trading rules entirely. The collar must be sized only to vested, unrestricted shares, because plan securities may never be hedged before vesting or while subject to a holding lock. The main traps are tenor and disclosure: forward contracts are given as an example of prohibited short-term dealing so the structure should run well beyond three months or be authorised by the NWL Board, and the arrangement must be entered in the personal Trading Register and disclosed in the annual declaration, with directors' and KMP interests published to the market where required.

summary: A funded collar is available to a2 Milk Directors and Senior Executives, but only with express prior written approval of both legs. Rule 6.9 names put and call options, equity swaps and arrangements varying economic risk in the Company's Securities, and permits them with prior written approval from the rule 7 approver (the Board for the Chair, the Chair for other Directors and the CEO, the Chair and CEO for Senior Executives); rule 6.10 separately permits granting a security interest or other encumbrance over Company Securities, and margin or securities lending, on advance notification plus written clearance, so the loan leg is not prohibited. Approval discretion is unfettered and clearance is revocable at any time and otherwise lasts ten trading days, so the trade must be entered promptly and the bank should provide for revoked clearance. Entry must sit outside the two blackout periods and any ad hoc period the Company specifies, and the arrangement should not look short term or speculative under rule 6.4. The policy says nothing about forced sales, margin calls or price triggers, so enforcement mechanics and any blackout-period settlement risk must be handled contractually, with only the 2 business day exceptional circumstances waiver in rule 6.5 as relief.

summary: A funded collar is not possible for any Breville director or executive. Section 5.1 prohibits every Employee from entering into any agreement, arrangement or scheme, including options, hedging arrangements or other Derivative products, that changes their economic benefit or risk in any holding of Breville shares or in an equity incentive award, and the defined term Derivative expressly names 'cap and collar'; the ban covers vested and unvested holdings alike, applies to all staff rather than only Restricted Persons, and has no approval, waiver or exceptional-circumstances route. Short-dated structures are separately barred by the section 5.2 three-month short-term trading rule, which names forward contracts, and Restricted Persons may not lend their Breville Securities to any party for any purpose, which blocks rehypothecation of collateral. Only the funding leg is available: including Breville Securities in a margin loan portfolio or similar funding arrangement requires the Chair's prior approval under section 4.6, and an involuntary disposal by an approved financier exercising its rights is an excluded dealing under section 6(e), even in a Closed Period. A bank could therefore offer an approved secured loan against Breville shares, but not the put and call legs that would make it a collar.
